# Elite duels: what helps in 1v1

**Data:** AI_Test `ctf-elite-duels-v3` (commit `abd4f7c99727`). 31 bots × 2,000 frozen duels against Player5, Astra, Sol, Fable, Sonnet and Opus (about 333 each; seats alternate; every fixture its own map).

**Tables:** in [DUEL_TABLES.md](DUEL_TABLES.md), generated by `tools/duel_review.py`.

## Duel play is deterministic: 31 bots are 9 behaviors

Bots sharing a duel code path produce identical results on all 2,000 fixtures, so there is no run-to-run noise. The only uncertainty is how well 2,000 maps represent others.

| Behavior | Bots |
|---|---|
| Control_Hybrid duel planner | 9 bots, **including Player2 v005**, the foundation, weights, CDP, DROP and FLAGS builds |
| Omega (Hybrid + endgame decay) | 13 bots: every Omega and gene build, Astra_Joint/Carrier, R3_CL_terminal |
| CFL | C12 |
| R3 expectimax (duel refinement) | C17, C18 |
| Astra habits | Astra_Habits, Astra_Full |
| R3 habits | C20 |
| ESCORT / HEALTHY / both | C16 / C21 / C15 |

Player2's lead at other team counts therefore does not come from duels; its duel play is Hybrid's exactly. All search genes (RISK, SH, ASYM, PLAYOUT) are inactive in duels.

## Results (win % with ties as half; Δ = paired points vs Hybrid)

| Behavior | Win % | Δ | vs Player5 | vs Astra | vs Sol | vs Fable / Sonnet / Opus |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| **CFL** | **77.6** | **+2.5 `+`** | **+8.5 `++`** | +4.0 | +1.4 | ≈ 0 |
| R3 expectimax | 76.9 | +1.7 | +5.8 `+` | **+6.4 `+`** | -0.9 | ≈ 0 |
| ESCORT | 75.3 | +0.1 | | | | |
| Omega | 75.2 | +0.1 (2 fixtures) | | | | |
| **Hybrid (control)** | **75.1** | — | 67.7 | 46.0 | 48.0 | 97.0 / 96.4 / 95.9 |
| Astra habits | 75.1 | 0.0 | +5.4 `+` | -3.0 | -0.8 | -0.9 / +0.2 / -1.1 |
| R3 habits | 75.1 | -0.1 | +5.2 `+` | -3.1 | -0.9 | similar |
| ESCORT + HEALTHY, HEALTHY | 75.0–75.1 | -0.1 | | | | |

## Findings

1. **CFL is confirmed in duels against strong opponents.** It is the best duel behavior, +2.5 points overall, with most of the gain against Player5 (+8.5). This matches the earlier benchmark, where CFL won every duel against Baseline. CFL should be on at 2 teams. At 3+ teams the earlier data says keep it off.
2. **The duel ceiling is Astra and Sol.** The control loses 453 of 2,000 duels:

   | Opponent | Losses | Win rate |
   |---|---:|---:|
   | Astra | 170 | about 46% |
   | Sol | 161 | about 48% |
   | Player5 | 93 | 68% |
   | Fable, Sonnet, Opus together | 29 | ≥96% |

   Further duel gains can only come against Astra and Sol.
3. **R3 expectimax is the only change that helps against Astra** (+6.4). CFL and expectimax fix partly different duels: each turns about 235 of the control's results into wins, 145 of them shared, and each also loses 173–194. A build combining CFL with the expectimax duel refinement is the obvious next test. Picking the better of the two per fixture would reach 86%, an upper bound only.
4. **Habit models help against Player5 (+5.4) but hurt against Astra (-3.0); net zero.** Against Baseline they cost 8–9 points. Opponent modeling clearly moves duel results opponent by opponent, but the online habit mixtures adapt the wrong way against Astra. Keep them off in duels.
5. **Duel results are chaotic but deterministic.** CFL changes the outcome of 409 of 2,000 duels to gain a net 63. Small planner changes reshuffle many games, so only paired tests on many maps can rank duel variants.

## Implications

- **Next heuristic control:** CFL on at 2 teams; then test CFL + R3 expectimax duel refinement against Astra and Sol specifically.
- **Neural plan:** the earlier advice to leave duels alone was based on Baseline-only data. Against elites, opponent modeling changes results per opponent (habits: +5.4 vs Player5, -3.0 vs Astra). That makes a learned duel opponent model (P for 2 teams, `n02`) worth trying, gated as everywhere: α = 0 unless it beats the forecast on held-out duels.
- **Rating weight:** duels are 1 of the 14 rated team counts. +2.5 points in duels is worth about +0.2 points on the all-sizes rating.
